diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose $\mu$ is a probability measure containing $S$ in its support and satisfying the following regularity assumptions

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem introduces μ but then uses an undefined measure ν in the Gram matrix and in supp(ν). No assumptions are given for ν, so the quantities G and γ are undefined. Additionally the index d is undefined (should likely be n).

failure_location.quote: with Gram matrix $G=\bmat{\inr{p_j}{p_k}_\nu}_{0\le j,k\le n}$ and max norm $\gamma=\max_{0\le j\le d}\magn{p_j(z)}_{\supp(\nu)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ν by the already introduced μ (and d by n), or introduce ν with its own explicit assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem a10 is ill-posed as written and cannot be applied.
issues.title: Undefined measure ν in Theorem a10
issues.why_classification: The statement is ill-posed, but the likely intended correction is a local replacement of the undefined measure; the main mathematical content can survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The inner product is defined without complex conjugation. For complex-valued polynomials or complex nodes, a^*Ga = ∫ L_k^2 dν, not ∫ |L_k|^2 dν. Thus the equality and the subsequent use of G^{-1} are invalid; G need not be positive definite. This undermines the proof of Lemma a18 and its application in Theorem a10.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the inner product as <f,g>_ν = ∫ f \bar g dν (with Hermitian Gram matrix), or restrict the theorem to real polynomials and real support points where L_k is real.
issues.overall_effect: The bounds on ||V^{-1}|| in Lemma a18 and the general theorem a10 are not established for complex polynomials/support points.
issues.title: Missing complex conjugation in Gram inner product
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the central inequality in Lemma a18 for the complex setting advertised by Theorem a10; repairing requires changing the inner product definition and reworking the bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis as written is dimensionally incorrect and does not ensure that the interval [nε+ε, 2π−ε] is nonempty. The intended condition is nε < 2π − 2√ε (or similar), which is needed for the denominator in ξ and for the proof's integration region.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis with the intended geometric condition nε < 2π − 2√ε (or (n+2)ε<2π) needed for the proof.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a21 and its use in the lower bound for equispaced nodes are not justified under the stated hypothesis.
issues.title: Incorrect hypothesis in Lemma a21
issues.why_classification: A single hypothesis correction restores the lemma; the mathematical content is otherwise unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Using the paper's definition, at α=1/2 the numerator is Cl(π/2)=G≈0.916, while the denominator is (1/4)log4≈0.3466, giving a ratio ≈2.64. This is far outside the claimed interval [1/π,2/5]≈[0.318,0.4]. The inequality is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the interval by a correct bound on the ratio (or simply assert it is bounded between positive constants) and adjust constants in Lemma a30.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bound is false. The proof of Lemma a30 uses this incorrect interval to bound M_n/M_w, though the final asymptotic statement can likely be recovered with corrected constants.
issues.title: False range for Clausen ratio in Proposition a24
issues.why_classification: The false inequality is a local constant error; the downstream estimates only need boundedness of the ratio, so the main results survive with adjusted constants.

issues.failure_explanation: With x=√M_n D and D=π−εn/2−ε, the displayed inequality is equivalent to erf(x) ≥ x/√(x^2 + D/π). For small x (which occurs for allowed parameters, e.g. ε=O(1)), this fails; for instance x=0.5, D=1 gives erf(0.5)≈0.520 < 0.5/√(0.25+1/π)≈0.664. Thus the proof's derivation of the lower bound in Lemma a42 is invalid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the error-function inequality with a valid lower bound (possibly with a larger absolute constant C) or add the missing small-x case analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound in Lemma a42 and the downstream estimates that rely on it are not established by the given proof, although the statements may be repairable with a different constant.
issues.title: Invalid error-function lower bound in Lemma a42
issues.why_classification: The faulty step is a contained technical inequality; repairing it requires a nontrivial but local argument and may adjust constants, without necessarily changing the main asymptotic results.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lagrange polynomial L_k(z) is complex-valued when the nodes are complex. The logarithm is not a real-valued function as used; the potential identity holds for log|L_k(z)|. Thus the statement and proof are ill-defined unless absolute values are inserted.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace log L_k(z) by log|L_k(z)| throughout Lemma a50 and its proof.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a50 and its use in Theorem a10 are unreliable as written.
issues.title: Log of complex Lagrange polynomial instead of modulus
issues.why_classification: A single local correction (adding absolute values) repairs the statement and proof without changing the substantive bounds.
